prompt:
Create a CORRECT LOW FORWARD BITE animation of the attached ORIGINAL ASHVEIL cinder bear, same detailed crisp pixel art, very heavy four-legged bear anatomy, small round ears, short broad bear muzzle, ash-tipped charcoal/soot-brown fur, tiny tail. This is a BITE snapping at knee height ahead, NOT a roar upward. ALL noses stay aimed LOW straight along their row's direction. Do not lift the chin, throw the head backward, rotate face sideways out of the row or expose the face in the rear row. Keep the massive body planted and stretch NECK FORWARD/LOW instead of standing or rearing. Four stout legs, no extra limbs, no wolf/humanoid anatomy, no scenery/target/gore.

EXACTLY 4 rows x 4 columns, 16 original distinct new full-body sprites on transparent RGBA. Row1 FRONT facing bottom/viewer with muzzle centered toward bottom; row2 LEFT nose horizontally left; row3 RIGHT nose horizontally right; row4 BACK head toward top away from viewer, rump/tail nearest viewer and face hidden. Elevated three-quarter game camera, same body/head scale and identity. Every silhouette confined to CENTER 55 percent of its cell, with large clear transparent gutters; no neighboring overlap or clipping. No shadows/floor/grid/labels/text/checkerboard/effects.

Four distinct bite key poses left-to-right: 1 ANTICIPATION head draws slightly back but remains low and forward, jaw begins to part; 2 CONTACT body leans forward and neck stretches LOW directly ahead, mouth opens by LOWER JAW DROPPING DOWN beneath level muzzle (teeth visible in front/side views), muzzle never points skyward; 3 SNAP mouth closes almost shut, low head remains thrust forward beyond planted forepaws; 4 RECOVER low head retracts and closes jaw, planted four-footed neutral stance. Front row advances muzzle toward bottom, left row advances muzzle to left, right row to right; back row advances neck toward top and shoulders flatten while face stays hidden. For back frames it is CORRECT to hide teeth behind head/body; do NOT rotate the bear rightward to display an open mouth. Four poses must show actual low head/neck/jaw trajectory, not four variations of a roaring bear.
